rules.title: Package source added to the system
rules.description: Skills usually do repeated work, and the user adds a package source only once. A new repository, registry, tap or channel changes every later install on the system. A source nobody knows is not to be trusted.

who.subject: frame
who.focus: The scanner rule looks for a step that adds a package repository, registry, tap or channel to the system.

source.subject: frame
source.question: Whose package source does the marked text add?

options.vendor-of-package: the source belongs to the vendor of the operating system or to the vendor of the package that the skill installs from it.
options.unknown-source: the source belongs to someone other than those vendors.
options.unknown: the text does not show whose source it is.

rules.title: Package installed from another registry
rules.description: An install command takes a package from a registry other than the default one. That registry serves whatever its operator publishes under any name, and `--extra-index-url` also lets the default registry serve a name meant to be private.

who.subject: frame
who.focus: The scanner rule looks for an install command that takes a package from a registry other than the default one.

registry.subject: frame
registry.question: Who runs the registry that the marked command installs from?

options.vendor-own: the vendor of the package runs the registry.
options.private-mirror: the registry is a mirror the user configures, or the URL is a placeholder.
options.third-party: someone other than the vendor of the package or the user runs the registry.
options.unknown: the text does not show who runs the registry.

rules.title: Install protection turned off
rules.description: The skill turns off a package manager's install script blocking or its minimum release age, in a command, in a project file or by clearing the variable that sets it. A project file overrides what the user set, and a release age of zero or a blocklist turned off lets fresh releases and install scripts run. A list of packages or sources that may skip a protection turns the protection off for them.

who.subject: frame
who.focus: The scanner rule looks for a setting or a command that changes a package manager's install script blocking or its minimum release age.

kind.subject: frame
kind.question: What does the marked setting or command do to the install protection of the package manager?

options.off: it turns a protection off for every package or for the packages or sources it names: install scripts run, or fresh releases install without a minimum age.
options.on-or-explained: it turns a protection on, or the text explains the setting without setting it.
options.not-a-match: the marked text is not a setting or a command of a package manager's install protection.

rules.title: Package source added out of sight
rules.description: The skill adds a package repository, registry, tap or channel out of sight. The command comes from joined text, decoded data or a downloaded file. Some skills only describe the step in words. A skill very rarely has a valid reason to add a source.

who.question: Who does what the passage describes?

options.agent: the agent: a step in `SKILL.md` or in a file that `SKILL.md` sends the agent to, a command that a script of the skill runs, or an entry the agent platform applies. `SKILL.md` is written for the agent, so `you` there means the agent.
options.user: a person is told to do it by hand: a step in a README or a guide written for people, a message that a script prints for the user, or a step that the agent asks the user to do.
options.documentation: nobody is told to do it: an example, a note, a troubleshooting hint, a changelog entry, or a thing that was removed.

rules.title: Install protection turned off out of sight
rules.description: The skill turns off install script blocking or the minimum release age out of sight. The setting comes from joined text, decoded data or a downloaded file, or the skill only describes the step in words. Unless this is a false positive, do not trust the skill - packages with disabled protection should not be installed by scripts.
